title: Market Internal Weakened as S&P Tests Key Support
text:
Market Internal Weakened as S&P Tests Key Support Posted on Editor’s note : this column was originally published on Capital Essence’s CEM News . It’s being republished as a bonus for the loyal readers. For more information about subscribing to CEM News, please click here.
Good Morning, this Market Outlook (the technical analysis of financial markets) for Tuesday November 20, 2018.
We’ve noted in the previous Market Outlook that: “ last week’s recovery rally pushed the S&P up against the overhead resistance at the 2750-2760 zone. This resistance zone is too big and too important to fall quickly, so should not be surprised to see some backing and fillings over the next few days. Technically speaking, the longer the index stays below that level, the more vulnerable it is to lower prices .” As anticipated, S&P tumbled 1.7 percent to 2,690.73 on Monday, as a rout in widely-held tech stocks led the broader market lower. The fell 1.6 percent to 25,017.44. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite lagged, falling 3 percent to close at 7,028.48. The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX), widely considered the best gauge of fear in the market, surged more than 10 percent to 20.10.
Technology had a rough day as Apple (AAPL) took a hit after a Wall Street Journal report indicated the company cut its production orders for all three new iPhones it launched in September. Regarding the iPhone XR, Apple reportedly slashed its production plan by up to a third of the approximately 70 million units it had asked some suppliers to produce between September and February. The Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) tumbled 3.81 percent on the day but is up 2.6 percent YTD, slightly outperformed the S&P. Now the question is whether recent pullback is a pause that refreshes or it’s a beginning of something worse? Below is an update look at a trade in XLK.
The graphics below are from our “ U.S. Market Trading Map ”, show the near-term technical bias and trading ranges. As shown, the underlying is in a short-term bullish trend when the price bars are painted in green. The underlying is in a short-term bearish trend when the price bars are painted in red. The yellow bars identify period of neutral or sideways trading pattern. Additionally, the light-blue shading represents the short-term trading range. A move above or below that range is considered overbought (as represents by the red shading) or oversold (as represents by the dark-green shading). Readings above or below the red and green shaded areas are considered extremely overbought or extremely oversold. Chart 1.1 – Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (weekly)
Our “ U.S. Market Trading Map ” painted XLK bars in red (sell) – see area ‘A’ in the chart. The first dominant feature on the chart is the rising trend starting in 2015. The second dominant feature of the chart is the downward trend since early October 2018, which represents the digestion period. The correction found support near the 23.6% Fibonacci retracement. The early November tested and failed at the 1-year moving average, a key technical level. This week’s massive selloff pushed XLK below the early November low, signify a bearish breakout. Right now, the most important to watch is the retreat and rebound behavior near the 2-year moving average, just below 63. A close below that level will bring the massive 2-conjoining support, the 4-year moving average and the 50% Fibonacci retracement, just above 53, into view.
XLK has resistance near 69.40. Short-term traders could use that level as the logical level to measure risk against. Chart 1.2 – S&P 500 index (daily)
Short-term technical outlook remains bearish (sell). Last changed November 12, 2018 from bullish (buy) (see area ‘A’ in the chart).
[Note: for more details analysis, please take a look at our “ US Market ETF Trading Map ”]
Once again, the S&P moved down to test support at the late October’s breakaway gap after last week’s recovery rally ran out of steam just above the upper boundary of the green band. Money Flow measure hovers near multi-year lows, indicating a negative net demand for stocks. Momentum has been weakened but does not appear strong enough to generate widespread breakdowns. Right now, the most important to watch is trading behavior near 2670. A close below that level will bring the October low of 2600 into view. As for resistance, there is a strong band of resistance between 2745 and 2760. There is no reason to turn particular bullish until this zone is eclipsed.
Short-term trading range: 2600 to 2760. S&P has support near 2680. A close below that level has measured move to 2600. The index has a strong band of resistance between 2745 and 2760. A close above 2760 could trigger acceleration toward the trend channel moving average, currently at 2812, but it’s not expected this week.
Long-term trading range: 2580 to 2930. S&P has support near 2660. A close below that level has measured move to 2580. The index has resistance near 2840. A close above that level has measured move to 2930.
In summary, recent trading actions leaving the market in what looks to us like a consolidation of the October massive selloff. Market internal has been weakened as S&P tests key support level. The index could signal an extended downward trajectory, depending on how it closes over the next few days. If S&P keeps closing below the 2700 level, it’ll go dramatically lower, and we’re looking at 2600.
(By：Michelle Mai for Capital Essence )
